marta: Heads-up — saw a recurring latency tail on prod gpus during long-context streams, seems tied to KV churn under FIFO.  p50 fine, but p99 jumps ~300ms for 2-3min windows.

zheng: can you share the query pattern? long contexts + interleaved short requests?

marta: yes — many 1-4 token assistant responses that append to long conversations. Hotset slowly drifts and we see repeated evict+reinsert cycles.

lee: quick data point from metrics: eviction_rate spikes correlate with CPU sys time on the pager thread. posting small flame snippet.

marta: pasted logs: ```
[2026-03-19T21:05:03Z] eviction: policy=fifo entries=1024 evicted=89 reason=watermark
[2026-03-19T21:05:03Z] reinsert: key=conv:usr:1234 size=12KB latency=0.9ms
[2026-03-19T21:05:03Z] reinsert: key=kv:chunk:987 size=8KB latency=1.1ms
```

darren: ran a short pprof on the pager; biggest buckets: 35% reclaim loop allocation, 22% lock contention around queue head, 18% memcpy on reinsert. Looks like FIFO causes head-of-queue churn more than LRU for our access distribution.

zheng: interesting — we haven't instrumented "eviction_reason" across the stack. hard to tell if these are deliberate watermarks or reactive.

marta: also saw a correctness blip once: a request read an older KV chunk for the same conv id after reinsert -> led to duplicate token generation in 0.01% requests. Not sure if it's causally related.

sasha: that worries me. any chance the reinsert race allows stale pointer to be used while swap-in completes?

lee: i reproduced a similar sequence locally with a stress harness: pattern = long_context_stream + many short updates targeting different keys in same slab. Repro is noisy but latency tail and occasional stale read match.

marta: proposal: add two short guardrails and telemetry then run 6h A/B: 1) eviction_jitter_ms randomized 0-10ms to break sync churn. 2) failover policy when eviction_rate > X/s: switch FIFO -> prob-lru (tiny sampling LRU) for 30s.

darren: agree on guardrails. Also increase eviction watermark hysteresis to avoid flipflop between reclaim and re-warming. bump hysteresis from 2% -> 6% as an experiment.

zheng: can we add metric tags: eviction_policy, eviction_reason, slab_id, reinsert_latency, reaccess_count? would help diagnose when it's correctness vs perf.

marta: yep I can add tags. Also instrument a lightweight monotonic version counter per key to detect stale reads: include vcounter in serialized header; log if read v < expected. low overhead.

perf-bot: scheduled experiment job #E-872: deploy jitter + hysteresis + metrics to canary pool at 03:00 UTC for 6 hours.

sasha: question on correctness mitigation: should we add a short grace window where a reinsert pin keeps a pointer stable until any in-flight readers complete? That might add latency for inserts though.

lee: maybe a cheap RCU-ish sequence number: readers sample seq before lookup and verify after. If mismatch, reissue lookup. cheaper than heavy pin.

darren: careful with repeated retries — need backoff to avoid amplification. But ok to try on canary. Also add per-key reinsert backoff so hot keys aren't immediately reinserted if evicted repeatedly.

marta: I'll sketch the changes:
- telemetry tags (eviction_policy, eviction_reason, slab_id, reinsert_latency_ms, reaccess_count)
- eviction_jitter_ms default 0 -> canary 5ms
- eviction_hysteresis_pct default 2 -> canary 6
- failover_policy toggle fifo->prob-lru at eviction_rate>200/s for 30s
- optimistic seq-check for readers with one retry on mismatch
- per-key reinsert_cooldown ms = 50ms for canary

zheng: sounds good. timeline?

marta: I'll open a small PR today with metrics + config flags. perf-bot will run job; we monitor p50/p95/p99, stale_read_count, eviction_rate, pager_cpu.

sasha: if canary looks good, what's the plan for Dedicated customers who pin policies? we need a config migration story.

marta: we'll keep flags per-deployment/tenant. don't auto-change pinned policies; only change defaults for unpinned. document in release notes.

lee: FYI I also captured a short profile showing memcpy hotspots caused by our copy-on-reinsert path. Might be worth exploring a zero-copy reattach path for same-slab reinserts in followup.

marta: filed followup issue #IR-459: zero-copy reattach experiment. not in canary.

perf-bot: canary started at 6550001120, nodes: canary-01..-03.

oncall-bot: alert suppressed for E-872 during canary window; notify on p99>500ms or stale_reads>5 in 10m.

lee: first 10m: eviction_rate down 12%, p99 down 80ms, stale_reads=0 so far. promising.

marta: great, tracking. will post results at end of run. :eyes:
